mode.why: third-party short of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its object designs, its copy, its figures or its characters (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL

ignored.why: the English copy (a trading-psychology story: most people lose money, markets run on fear and greed, know your targets and risk, buy quality, master your mindset, save this post) and every figure in it (the account balance counting $47,275 down to $157, the 'My account' label) are third-party copy and claims; never reused as text, numbers or topic

the character designs (the sad sphere-headed bust, the crowd of sphere-headed figures with raised arms, the tiny stick figure on the account bar, the meditating glossy figure) are the creator's designs; our scenes take their subjects from the voice-over and only borrow the rendering style (glossy spheres, rim light, one colour per mood)

the 'Euphoria / Fear' chart with its 'Buy Quality' and 'Profit' pills is the reference's argument; only the technique (two labelled curves drawing themselves and crossing, dashed markers, a pointer stepping between pills) is borrowed, with our data and labels from the package
the audio track (voice and bed) is third-party; L2 uses our voice-over and L6 builds our sound

visual_language: A dark, glowing finance-psychology short told by one narrating voice whose words appear on screen one at a time. Medium: simple 3D-looking objects (glossy spheres as people, frosted glass chart cards, chrome coins, a glossy figure) and code-like charts, all floating in a pure black void and lit from inside or from a strong coloured light above. Two mood colours run the whole film: green means gain, calm, the right way; red means loss, fear, panic. Each scene is lit in one of them, and a scene can turn from one to the other in about half a second to show the mood flip. Typography: a small white neutral grotesk sans single-word caption at the top centre that changes with every spoken word (no sentence build, one word at a time), broken by pure-type shots where a sentence builds word by word in the middle of the frame (words fade from grey to white), sometimes with key words larger, condensed and colour-coded, or swung in in 3D. Rhythm: 11 shots in 31.6 s (about 2.9 s each), hard cuts on phrase boundaries, never on a beat; some cuts are carried by an object (an orb enters at the end of one shot and is the hero of the next, then flies out to begin the type that follows). Moves are smooth and slow on objects (self-drawing lines, slow orbits, a gentle crowd bob), fast on accents (counters ticking, glints riding line tips, speed streaks, short push-ins and pull-backs into cuts). Signature moments: the balance counting down while the card turns red; the whole crowd scene flipping from green to red at the peak; the glowing orb breaking through two slabs; two colour-coded giant words naming the forces.
look: 2.5D leaning to real 3D in a pure black studio void. Materials: glossy dark spheres with white rim light (people stand-ins), frosted glass cards with a faint grid and soft edge highlight, metallic green chrome coins with motion blur, a glossy green-to-white gradient figure, matte dark-green slabs. Light: a strong coloured volumetric light from the top edge (green or red) in the crowd scene, objects glowing from inside, rim lights from above, star-shaped cross-flare glints on line tips, a soft radial glow at a corner of the frame for type shots. Depth: shallow; objects mostly sit in one plane with soft perspective tilt, no heavy depth of field. Background: pure black most of the time, a dark grey diagonal gradient for two shots, a soft green radial glow with faint rings at the end.
code_translation: Mostly code-native with 3D accents. Per D55 the 3D parts are built as real 3D in code with three.js: glossy spheres and the figure with MeshPhysicalMaterial (low roughness, clearcoat) plus a white rim light from above; frosted glass cards as rounded boxes with transmission and roughness plus a grid texture and an emissive edge; chrome coins as cylinders with a metallic material and a horizontal motion-blur pass (or stretched copies with falling opacity); the coloured top light as a spot light plus an additive cone sprite. The mood flip is one tween on a shared colour uniform (light, emissive tints, glints, rims) from the brand's positive role to its warning role over about 0.4 s. Charts and counters are SVG or canvas: stroke-dashoffset line draws with an additive cross-flare sprite riding the tip, counters tweened with Persian digits and separators per data-viz.md. The single-word caption and the pure-type shots are HTML type in the brand Persian font, whole words only (rtl-grammar.md), timed from audio.json word times: words fade grey to white in about 0.15 s, key words larger and in the mood colour; the 3D swing-in uses CSS rotateY with perspective, the tightening CTA uses a letter-spacing tween on whole words (never on joined Persian letters one by one). The orb streak is a glowing sphere with a trail sprite and looping speed lines.
continuity: One word on screen at a time: a small caption at the top centre swaps with every spoken word, so the voice is always readable without covering the subject.
Two mood colours run the film: every scene is lit in the positive colour or the warning colour, never both at once, and the meaning of each colour never changes.
Mood flip in place: instead of cutting, the whole scene (light, glass, glints, figures) recolours from one mood to the other in about half a second while the subject keeps moving.
Object carries the cut: an object enters at the end of one shot, is the hero of the next, and flies out of frame to start the shot after it.
Push-in or pull-back into the cut: a short fast scale move on the subject right before a hard cut.
Glint on the tip: every data line draws itself with a star-shaped glint riding its head.
Breath shots of pure type: the story's key sentences leave the subject and sit alone in the middle of a dark frame, words building one by one, key words bigger or in colour.
Simple glossy stand-ins: people and ideas are shown by simple glossy spheres and solids with a rim light, never by detailed illustration.
Things appear on the spoken word: pills, icons, markers and pointers pop in or move exactly when the voice names them.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its trading-psychology story, English copy, figures (the $47,275 to $157 balance), its character designs (the sad sphere bust, the cheering crowd, the meditating figure), the 'Euphoria / Fear / Buy Quality / Profit' chart, its audio, or its shot order one by one.

Red and green as mood colours: map them onto the brand's positive and warning colour roles; if the brand bans either colour or has no warning role, keep the mood flip with brand-approved colours (L1). Colours were read by eye, not sampled.

The single-word top caption is small (cap height about 2% of frame height): in our film it must meet the minimum text size and hold times (a Persian word on screen for at least its spoken length and never under the brand minimum) and sit inside the safe zone (safe-zones.md); very short words may need to be grouped with the next word.
Word fades, 3D swings and the tightening CTA must use whole Persian words in a shaped font, placed right to left; joined letters are never split, spaced apart or rotated one by one (rtl-grammar.md).

The film's direction is left to right (lines draw left to right, the orb flies left to right, words enter from the left): in our RTL film time and progress run right to left unless a chart's convention says otherwise (rtl-grammar.md, data-viz.md).
Dark frames score low in scene detect: cuts were found only at a 0.06 threshold; 4.7 s, 9.7-10.2 s, 16.4 s and 28.4 s were read by eye (±0.1 s).
Audio is third-party voice and bed; ignored, L2 and L6 build ours. The film ends on its own CTA: ours ends with the package CTA and the brand logo outro.
